annotation.authors_or_issuer: International Working Group on Data Protection in Technology (IWGDPT)
annotation.venue: International Working Group on Data Protection in Technology (Berlin Group)
annotation.summary_en: Working paper of the International Working Group on Data Protection in Technology on smart cities. It sets out data protection principles across data collection, analysis and decision stages (IoT sensors, CCTV, drones, AI, profiling, digital twins) and gives recommendations to cities, industry and regulators. Collector metadata title refers to a different Canadian OPC document.
key_provisions_or_claims: Cities and partners should complete accountability and governance assessments, including DPIAs, before processing begins.
Cities should abstain from using data that is of poor quality or unrepresentative, to avoid discriminatory decisions.
Purpose limitation requires compatibility assessments before reusing data for new purposes.
Industry should provide security upgrades and vulnerability disclosure policies, and avoid universal default passwords.
Regulators should issue guidance on multi-actor governance, data minimisation and citizens' rights.
